    <div class="project-card featured">
      <div class="featured-body">
        <div class="project-type">R Package · Org: repro-stats</div>
        <h3>regulog — Tamper-Evident Audit Logging for R</h3>
        <p>
          A hash-chained, session-level audit logging system for regulated R environments.
          Every action, change, annotation, and signature is recorded in a tamper-evident
          chain — any post-hoc modification is detectable by <code>verify_log()</code>.
          Directly covers 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10, §11.100, §11.200 and EU Annex 11
          Clauses 9 and 11. Ships with IQ/OQ/PQ qualification scripts and a full
          Requirements Traceability Matrix.
        </p>
        <table class="module-table">
          <tr><th>Function</th><th>Purpose</th></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>log_action()</strong></td><td>Record a discrete analytical event with mandatory reason</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>log_change()</strong></td><td>Document before/after field modifications</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>log_note()</strong></td><td>Annotate decisions, outlier rationale, query resolutions</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>log_signature()</strong></td><td>Named, dated electronic sign-off per §11.100/§11.200</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>with_log()</strong></td><td>Auto-log all data I/O in a scoped block</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>verify_log()</strong></td><td>Recompute SHA-256 chain; report first broken entry</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>filter_log()</strong></td><td>Query entries by type, user, action, or date range</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>export_audit_trail()</strong></td><td>Export signed CSV or JSON for submission</td></tr>
        </table>

          <span class="tag">Shiny</span>

    <!-- lineager -->
    <div class="project-card featured">
      <div class="featured-body">
        <div class="project-type">R Package · Org: repro-stats</div>
        <h3>lineager — Row-Level Data Provenance and Exclusion Tracking</h3>
        <p>
          Tags every row with a unique lineage ID (<code>.__lid__</code>) that survives
          filters, joins, and derivations. Every row removal requires a documented reason.
          CDISC-aware: USUBJID embedded in lineage IDs; population flags and SDTM-to-ADaM
          derivations registerable via <code>lg_population()</code> and <code>lg_spec()</code>.
          Generates CDISC Reviewer's Guide-aligned HTML provenance reports.
        </p>
        <table class="module-table">
          <tr><th>Function</th><th>Purpose</th></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>lg_tag()</strong></td><td>Assign row-level lineage IDs to source datasets</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>lg_filter()</strong></td><td>Tracked filter with mandatory exclusion reason</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>lg_derive()</strong></td><td>Tracked mutate with documented description</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>lg_join()</strong></td><td>Tracked join with bilateral row-ID tracing</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>lg_trace()</strong></td><td>Trace any subject across the complete pipeline</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>lg_exclusions()</strong></td><td>Full exclusion registry with reasons and populations</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>lg_disposition()</strong></td><td>CONSORT-style disposition table</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>lg_lineage() / lg_plot()</strong></td><td>Pipeline lineage graph (Graphviz DOT)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>lg_report()</strong></td><td>Self-contained HTML provenance report</td></tr>
        </table>

        <h3>bayprior — Bayesian Prior Elicitation for Clinical Trials</h3>
        <p>
          An advanced R package and Shiny application for Bayesian prior elicitation,
          conflict diagnostics, and sensitivity analysis in clinical trials. Addresses the
          upstream problem that existing Bayesian trial packages largely ignore: how to
          construct, validate, and justify a prior to a regulator — directly aligned with
          the FDA's 2026 draft guidance on Bayesian methods.
        </p>
        <table class="module-table">
          <tr><th>Module</th><th>What it does</th></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Prior Elicitation</strong></td><td>SHELF roulette, quantile &amp; moment matching across Beta, Normal, Gamma, Log-Normal, Exponential, Weibull</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Expert Pooling</strong></td><td>Linear &amp; logarithmic pooling with Bhattacharyya diagnostics</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Conflict Diagnostics</strong></td><td>Box p-value, surprise index, KL divergence for binary, continuous, Poisson, and survival data</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Sensitivity Analysis</strong></td><td>Hyperparameter grids, tornado plots, influence heatmaps</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Robust &amp; Power Priors</strong></td><td>Sceptical, robust mixture (Schmidli et al.), and power priors (Ibrahim–Chen)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><strong>Regulatory Reports</strong></td><td>Self-contained HTML, PDF, or Word reports aligned with FDA/EMA expectations, rendered via Quarto</td></tr>
        </table>

    <!-- reproducr -->
    <div class="project-card featured">
      <div class="featured-body">
        <div class="project-type">R Package · Org: repro-stats · CRAN</div>
        <h3>reproducr — Behavioural Reproducibility Auditing for R</h3>
        <p>
          <code>reproducr</code> makes the hidden risks of long-lived R analyses visible and trackable.
          Package updates can silently change function behaviour; stochastic code without a fixed seed
          produces different results on every run; locale-sensitive operations behave differently across
          systems. <code>reproducr</code> surfaces all of this — before results reach a journal, a regulator,
          or a collaborator. Works with or without <code>renv</code>; no configuration required.
        </p>
        <table class="module-table">
          <tr><th colspan="3">Three-tier workflow</th></tr>
          <tr><th>Function</th><th>Tier</th><th>Purpose</th></tr>
          <tr><td><code>audit_script()</code></td><td><span class="tier-badge">1</span></td><td>Extract all pkg::fn calls with version info; flag missing seeds &amp; locale-sensitive ops</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>risk_score()</code></td><td><span class="tier-badge">1</span></td><td>Score calls against a curated breaking-changes database (13 packages, 30+ entries)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>certify()</code></td><td><span class="tier-badge">2</span></td><td>Hash and store analytical outputs (coefficients, p-values, N) as a signed baseline</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>check_drift()</code></td><td><span class="tier-badge">2</span></td><td>Detect numerical drift between current outputs and any stored baseline</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>repro_report()</code></td><td><span class="tier-badge">3</span></td><td>Render audit report — minimal, academic methods paragraph, or pharma QC with sign-off fields</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>repro_badge()</code></td><td><span class="tier-badge">3</span></td><td>Generate a live shields.io reproducibility badge; CI updates it on every push</td></tr>
        </table>
        <div class="project-tags" style="margin-top:1rem;">

          <span class="tag tag-teal">repro-stats org</span>
